desc-calc-too-narrow.draft: This course covers functions, limits and continuity, the derivative and its differentiation rules, the chain rule and implicit differentiation, higher-order derivatives, related rates and optimization problems in engineering.

ref-calc-relevant.label: ALIGNED
ref-calc-relevant.sourceQuote: Chapters on limits, derivatives and their applications.
ref-calc-relevant.explanation: A calculus text on limits, derivatives and applications supports the weekly topics.

ref-calc-older-foundational.label: ALIGNED
ref-calc-older-foundational.sourceQuote: A classic text on limits, continuity and differentiation.
ref-calc-older-foundational.explanation: The analysis text covers limits, continuity and differentiation, matching the listed weeks. It is older and more advanced, but it is still relevant.

ref-calc-unrelated.label: NOT_ALIGNED
ref-calc-unrelated.explanation: The page is about cooking with garden herbs, which has nothing to do with differential calculus. It cannot support the weekly topics on limits of a function, the derivative or differentiation rules, so it cannot support the course.
ref-calc-unrelated.draft: Replace this reference with a calculus text or page covering limits, derivatives and differentiation rules, for example a university-level differential calculus textbook chapter.

clo-po-prog-aligned.label: ALIGNED
clo-po-prog-aligned.targetQuote: Design, implement and test object-oriented programs
clo-po-prog-aligned.explanation: CLO has design and implement of programs, at Create level, matching the PO.

clo-po-prog-lower-level.label: NOT_ALIGNED
clo-po-prog-lower-level.sourceQuote: Design and evaluate computing solutions for real problems.
clo-po-prog-lower-level.targetQuote: List the keywords of the programming language.
clo-po-prog-lower-level.explanation: The CLO only asks to list keywords (Remember), while the PO asks for design and evaluate (Create/Evaluate). Neither verb appears, and the object (keywords of a language) is not computing solutions for real problems.
clo-po-prog-lower-level.draft: Design and evaluate object-oriented program solutions for real problems, using the constructs of the programming language.

clo-po-prog-two-skills.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
clo-po-prog-two-skills.sourceQuote: communicate them effectively to technical and non-technical audiences
clo-po-prog-two-skills.targetQuote: Design a program solution for a given problem.
clo-po-prog-two-skills.explanation: The CLO shows design of a program solution, but the PO's second skill, communicating solutions effectively to technical and non-technical audiences, is missing.
clo-po-prog-two-skills.draft: Design a program solution for a given problem and communicate it effectively to technical and non-technical audiences through documentation and a demonstration.

clo-po-prog-interdisciplinary.label: ALIGNED
clo-po-prog-interdisciplinary.sourceQuote: Analyze the impact of computing on individuals
clo-po-prog-interdisciplinary.targetQuote: Evaluate the ethical and social implications of a software system
clo-po-prog-interdisciplinary.explanation: CLO evaluates ethical and social implications of software on users, which matches analyzing computing's impact on individuals and society at an equal or higher level.

clo-ega-aligned.label: ALIGNED
clo-ega-aligned.targetQuote: Analyze alternative designs and justify the selection
clo-ega-aligned.explanation: Analyzing alternatives and justifying a choice shows critical and creative thinking.

clo-ega-unrelated.label: NOT_ALIGNED
clo-ega-unrelated.targetQuote: Recite the history of the institution.
clo-ega-unrelated.explanation: Reciting institutional history is Remember level, has no professional competence in programming, and its subject is unrelated to the course.
clo-ega-unrelated.draft: Develop and test object-oriented programs that meet professional standards of correctness and code quality for given problems.

ilo-clo-prog-aligned.label: ALIGNED
ilo-clo-prog-aligned.targetQuote: Implement a class hierarchy using inheritance
ilo-clo-prog-aligned.explanation: Implementing an inheritance hierarchy is a smaller step of the CLO's implement component, in the same subject.

ilo-activity-prog-practises.label: ALIGNED
ilo-activity-prog-practises.sourceQuote: Implement a class hierarchy using inheritance
ilo-activity-prog-practises.targetQuote: Students code a class hierarchy in the laboratory
ilo-activity-prog-practises.explanation: Students code a class hierarchy in lab, practising implementation with feedback.

ilo-assess-prog-aligned.label: ALIGNED
ilo-assess-prog-aligned.targetQuote: submit an entity-relationship diagram and a normalized schema
ilo-assess-prog-aligned.explanation: The project requires an ER diagram and normalized schema, scored by rubric, which is evidence of design.

ilo-assess-prog-mcq-for-design.label: NOT_ALIGNED
ilo-assess-prog-mcq-for-design.sourceQuote: Design a normalized database schema for a given scenario.
ilo-assess-prog-mcq-for-design.explanation: A multiple-choice quiz on terms collects recall (Remember) evidence only. It does not show design, the schema being produced, or normalization applied to a scenario.
ilo-assess-prog-mcq-for-design.draft: Project: students design and submit an entity-relationship diagram and a normalized schema for an assigned scenario, scored with a rubric.

ilo-assess-named-only.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
ilo-assess-named-only.explanation: The task is only named 'Quiz'. It does not say what is asked or produced, nor that students explain recursion, such as how a base case and recursive case work.
ilo-assess-named-only.draft: Quiz: students answer short-answer questions explaining recursion, including the base case and recursive case, and trace a simple recursive method.

ilo-assess-mcq-for-understand.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
ilo-assess-mcq-for-understand.sourceQuote: Describe the difference between a stack and a queue.
ilo-assess-mcq-for-understand.targetQuote: Multiple-choice quiz on data structure concepts.
ilo-assess-mcq-for-understand.explanation: Multiple choice can support Understand, but the task names only 'concepts' and does not state that stacks and queues are compared. The describe-the-difference evidence is not clear.
ilo-assess-mcq-for-understand.draft: Multiple-choice quiz on stacks and queues, with items asking students to identify the difference in ordering (LIFO vs FIFO) and the operations of each, plus a short written item describing the difference.

clo-po-nurs-aligned.label: ALIGNED
clo-po-nurs-aligned.sourceQuote: Provide safe, quality nursing care to individuals using the nursing process
clo-po-nurs-aligned.targetQuote: Perform basic nursing procedures safely using the nursing process
clo-po-nurs-aligned.explanation: The CLO performs nursing procedures safely using the nursing process, matching the PO's safe care with the nursing process at an Apply level.

clo-po-nurs-unrelated.label: NOT_ALIGNED
clo-po-nurs-unrelated.sourceQuote: Provide safe, quality nursing care to individuals using the nursing process.
clo-po-nurs-unrelated.targetQuote: Compute the derivative of polynomial functions.
clo-po-nurs-unrelated.explanation: The CLO is about calculus. It has no nursing care verb, no safety or nursing process, and the wrong subject, so it fails tests 1 and 3. It also does not belong to this nursing course. The draft restores the course's own CLO.
clo-po-nurs-unrelated.draft: Perform basic nursing procedures safely using the nursing process on a simulated patient.

ilo-activity-nurs-practises.label: ALIGNED
ilo-activity-nurs-practises.sourceQuote: Demonstrate the correct procedure for taking blood pressure
ilo-activity-nurs-practises.targetQuote: Return demonstration of blood pressure measurement on a partner
ilo-activity-nurs-practises.explanation: Students do a return demonstration of blood pressure measurement, practising the verb 'demonstrate' on the same subject.

ilo-assess-nurs-knowledge-for-skill.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
ilo-assess-nurs-knowledge-for-skill.sourceQuote: Perform hand hygiene using the correct technique.
ilo-assess-nurs-knowledge-for-skill.targetQuote: Written exam on the steps of hand hygiene.
ilo-assess-nurs-knowledge-for-skill.explanation: The ILO asks students to perform hand hygiene with correct technique (Apply). A written exam on the steps only collects recall or understanding evidence. It does not show that students can perform the technique, so it fails tests 1 and 2. The subject is right, but the product is a written answer, not an observed performance.
ilo-assess-nurs-knowledge-for-skill.draft: Return demonstration of hand hygiene in the skills laboratory, scored by the instructor with a checklist of the correct technique (palm-to-palm, between fingers, thumbs, fingertips, 20 seconds, drying). A short written quiz on the steps supports it.
